productName: Rainbow AI — FnB Widget Bug Fixes (Image 3 + Image 4)
overview: Fix two critical bugs visible in screenshots: (1) hostel fallback text appearing in makan-moments cafe widget (UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_MESSAGES hardcoded hostel text), (2) raw JSON object rendered in chat bubble instead of plain text (chatWithToolsLoop returns unguarded LLM content). Also fix webchat-api not injecting FnB tools and unicode corruption in system prompt.
goals: Fix Image 3: hostel fallback text ('bookings, check-in/out, amenities') never appears in makan-moments widget
Fix Image 4: raw JSON '{"intent":...}' never rendered in chat bubble — chatWithToolsLoop sanitizes LLM output
Fix webchat-api tool injection: /chat/makan-moments widget gets FnB tool-calling capability
Fix unicode corruption in system prompt (em dash + rainbow emoji garbled)
Graceful tool-failure fallback: if FNB_MCP_URL is down, AI gives a helpful answer instead of hostel fallback
Regression tests for both image bugs

userStories.title: Fix hostel fallback text appearing in makan-moments AI waiter
userStories.description: UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_MESSAGES.en in ai-response-generator.ts is hardcoded as 'I can help with bookings, check-in/out, amenities, and general hostel information.' When chatWithToolsLoop exhausts its 3 loops (e.g. FNB_MCP_URL is down), this hostel-specific text is returned to the makan-moments cafe widget (Image 3 bug). Fix by adding per-profile fallback support: read unknownFallback from the profile's settings.json so each profile can override the default, and set makan-moments to a cafe-appropriate fallback.

userStories.title: Fix raw JSON displayed in chat widget when LLM returns JSON format
userStories.description: chatWithToolsLoop returns the raw LLM content string without checking if it is JSON. When the LLM responds in the old structured format {'intent':'menu_query','action':'llm_reply','response':'...','confidence':0.0}, the entire JSON string is sent to the chat widget and rendered verbatim (Image 4 bug). Fix: add a looksLikeJson guard in chatWithToolsLoop — if content looks like JSON, try to extract the 'response' or 'text' field; if none found, use the profile fallback.
acceptanceCriteria: chatWithToolsLoop never returns a string starting with '{' to the caller
If LLM content is valid JSON with a 'response' or 'text' string field, that field value is returned
If JSON has no extractable text, profile-aware fallback is returned instead
Test: mock chatWithFallback to return '{"intent":"menu_query","response":"Test reply","confidence":0.5}' — chatWithToolsLoop must return 'Test reply'
npm run build passes
technicalNotes: Edit src/assistant/ai-response-generator.ts: in chatWithToolsLoop, at line 141 where `return content || UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_MESSAGES.en`, add guard: if (content && looksLikeJson(content)) { try { const j = JSON.parse(content); const extracted = j.response || j.text || j.message || null; if (extracted && typeof extracted === 'string' && !looksLikeJson(extracted)) return extracted; } catch {} return UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_MESSAGES.en; } return content || UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_MESSAGES.en

Also apply the same guard at line 182 (max loops exhausted last content): before returning UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_MESSAGES.en, check if the last message in messages has content that looks like JSON and try to extract from it.

userStories.title: Inject FnB tools into webchat-api for makan-moments profile
userStories.description: webchat-api.ts (/api/chat/:profileId/message) calls processChat() WITHOUT tools for ALL profiles. This means the embedded rainbow-ai widget at /chat/makan-moments cannot use FnB tools (menu lookup, order placement). Fix: when profileId === 'makan-moments', pass toolRegistry.getToolsForProfile('makan-moments') and toolRegistry.getHandlersForProfile('makan-moments') to processChat().

technicalNotes: Edit src/routes/public/webchat-api.ts: add import { toolRegistry } from '../../tools/registry.js'. In the POST handler, after resolving profile, before calling processChat(), add: const fnbTools = profileId === 'makan-moments' ? toolRegistry.getToolsForProfile('makan-moments') : []; const fnbHandlers = profileId === 'makan-moments' ? toolRegistry.getHandlersForProfile('makan-moments') : new Map(); Then add tools: fnbTools, toolHandlers: fnbHandlers to the processChat() call.

userStories.title: chatWithToolsLoop graceful fallback: answer without tools if all tool calls fail
userStories.description: When FNB_MCP_URL is unavailable, every tool call in chatWithToolsLoop returns an error. The LLM sees 3 rounds of error responses and finally exhausts max loops, returning an unhelpful fallback. Fix: track if ALL tool calls across loops failed. If so, make one final LLM call WITHOUT tools (just the conversation) to get at least a helpful general response, before falling back to the profile fallback text.
acceptanceCriteria: When all tool results have isError:true, chatWithToolsLoop makes a final toolless LLM call

npm run build passes
technicalNotes: Edit src/assistant/ai-response-generator.ts chatWithToolsLoop: add a boolean allToolsFailed = false. After the loop, if all tool calls had isError:true (track with a counter), make one extra call: const { content: finalContent } = await chatWithFallback(messages.filter(m => m.role !== 'tool'), maxTokens, temp, false, undefined, undefined). Return finalContent if truthy and not JSON. The messages filtered are the original without tool results.

userStories.title: Profile-scoped admin tab URLs: every tab includes profileId in hash
userStories.description: The admin panel URL only encodes the tab name (e.g. #intents, #responses) but never the active profile. Switching from hostel to cafe profile only updates localStorage — the URL stays the same. This causes cross-profile data bleed: a user on #intents may see hostel intents instead of cafe intents because the API calls use a stale x-profile-id header. Fix: update all profile-specific tabs to include profileId in the URL (#intents/makan-moments, #responses/pelangi, etc.) following the pattern already used by #dashboard/makan-moments/tests. Switching profiles updates the URL; loading a URL auto-switches to the correct profile. Global tabs (settings, whatsapp, staff-review, help) keep the current flat URL.

Navigating to #intents/pelangi auto-switches to pelangi profile and loads hostel intents

Tabs that are profile-specific update their URL on load if profileId is missing (redirect #intents → #intents/activeProfileId)
Global tabs (settings, whatsapp, staff-review, help, live-chat) do NOT get a profileId in the URL
Profile-specific tabs: dashboard, intents, understanding, responses, performance, chat-simulator, tests, knowledge-base, workflows
Refreshing the page restores both the tab and the profile from the URL
getTabInfoFromUrl() returns {main, profileId, sub} — profileId is parts[1] if it matches a known profile ID, else null

Sub becomes parts[2] when profileId is present.

userStories.title: WCAG 2.1 AA keyboard accessibility for webchat widget
userStories.description: The webchat widget lacks required ARIA attributes and keyboard navigation support, blocking screen reader users and violating WCAG 2.1 AA. The message container needs role='log' for screen reader announcements, the toggle button needs aria-expanded, the input needs aria-label, and focus must be trapped inside the open panel with Escape-to-close.

Pressing Escape closes the panel and returns focus to the toggle button
Send button has aria-label='Send message'
New AI messages are announced by screen readers via the aria-live region

Add GET /api/admin/conversations/search?q=&profileId= endpoint

userStories.title: Template variable interpolation in static reply messages ({{guestName}}, etc.)
userStories.description: Static replies send fixed text strings with no personalization. Support for template variables like {{guestName}}, {{checkInDate}}, and {{profileName}} would allow staff to create personalized automated responses without LLM calls, improving quality while keeping latency near zero for common greetings and confirmations.
acceptanceCriteria: Static reply templates can include {{variableName}} placeholders in their text content
On send, available variables (guestName, checkInDate, checkOutDate, profileName) are resolved from session context
Unresolvable variables fall back to an empty string or configurable default (e.g., 'our valued guest')
Admin editor shows a popover listing supported {{variables}} when editing a static reply text field
Variable substitution is applied before the message is sent; the raw template is stored in the config
Existing static replies without variables continue to work unchanged
technicalNotes: Implement an interpolate(template: string, variables: Record<string, string>) utility in src/assistant/
Variable context: profileName from settings.json; guest data from active session if tool result is available
Apply interpolation in the static_reply action handler just before message delivery
Admin UI change: add a help tooltip showing {{guestName}}, {{checkInDate}}, {{profileName}} as supported vars

userStories.title: Server-Sent Events streaming for progressive AI responses in webchat widget
userStories.description: The webchat widget waits for the full AI response before displaying it, causing a blank 3-10 second wait. Industry best practice is to stream AI tokens progressively using SSE or chunked transfer, reducing perceived latency to near-instant first-token display. Both OpenRouter and NVIDIA providers support OpenAI-compatible streaming.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/chat/:profileId/message returns a streaming SSE response for LLM-generated replies
The webchat.html renders tokens as they arrive, appending to the current assistant message bubble
A typing indicator (animated dots) is shown from message submission until the first token arrives
Streaming falls back gracefully to non-streaming single response if the provider does not support it
Static replies (pre-written responses) return instantly with no streaming overhead
Streaming works correctly with tool calls: tools execute server-side, then response text streams after
technicalNotes: Use EventSource (SSE) on client with text/event-stream content type on server
OpenRouter streaming: add stream: true to completions request, pipe response chunks as SSE events
NVIDIA NIM/Kimi K2.5 supports OpenAI-compatible streaming via the same stream: true flag
Tool calls must complete before streaming text phase begins (tool results are not streamed to client)
Add X-Accel-Buffering: no header for Nginx proxy compatibility with SSE

userStories.title: Complete webhook event routing to registered notification handlers
userStories.description: The webhook routing code in src/routes/webhooks/index.ts has TODO comments indicating that event-type routing and handler dispatch are not implemented. Inbound webhook events from external systems are received by the server but silently dropped with no handler execution, making the webhook integration feature non-functional.
acceptanceCriteria: Inbound webhook POST requests are dispatched to the correct handler function based on the event type field
A handler registry maps event type strings to async handler functions (at minimum one working handler)
Unrecognized event types return HTTP 422 with a descriptive error message and are logged
Handler errors are caught, logged, and return HTTP 500 without crashing the Express server
HMAC signature verification is enforced for all inbound webhook requests (or clearly documented as not required)
Vitest unit tests cover: correct handler dispatch, unrecognized event 422 response, and handler error 500 response
technicalNotes: Remove TODO comments in src/routes/webhooks/index.ts and implement a handler dispatch map
Follow existing route patterns in src/routes/admin/ for consistent error handling and response shapes
Add WEBHOOK_SECRET env var for HMAC-SHA256 signature verification if not already present
Implement at minimum a payment_confirmed handler that sends a WhatsApp confirmation message

userStories.title: Sentiment-based early escalation trigger in message processing pipeline
userStories.description: Current escalation triggers are intent-based, requiring users to explicitly request help. Frustrated or angry language is not detected, meaning the bot continues attempting to handle the situation without proactive human handoff. A lightweight sentiment check before intent classification enables early escalation before frustration peaks.
acceptanceCriteria: Messages containing strong negative sentiment markers are detected in the pipeline before intent classification
If a user sends 3 or more messages with negative sentiment in a single session, the pipeline escalates to human
The escalation message to the user is empathetic and acknowledges frustration (configurable per profile)
Sentiment detection can be enabled or disabled per profile in admin settings
Sentiment-triggered escalation events are recorded in escalation_events table with reason='sentiment'
Sentiment detection does not add more than 50ms to the average message processing time
technicalNotes: Use a rule-based keyword/phrase list (not a separate LLM call) to avoid latency and cost
Initial negative marker set (EN): 'useless', 'terrible', 'awful', 'angry', 'never again', repeated '!!', 'ridiculous'
Track consecutive_negative_messages counter in session context (in-memory, not persisted to DB)
Add sentiment_escalation_enabled and sentiment_threshold to profile settings.json
Optional: include sentiment as a classified field in existing intent classification LLM prompt to avoid extra round-trip

userStories.title: Restore prior conversation history on webchat widget page reload
userStories.description: When a user reloads the page or navigates away and returns to the webchat, the conversation history disappears even though a sessionId is stored in localStorage. Re-fetching and rendering prior messages on load reduces user frustration from having to repeat their queries and provides a professional chat experience.
acceptanceCriteria: On widget initialization, if a sessionId exists in localStorage, the last 10 messages are fetched from the server
Fetched messages are rendered in the chat UI in chronological order before the input is enabled
A subtle visual divider labeled 'Previous conversation' separates restored history from the current session
History fetch fails gracefully: if the endpoint errors, the widget opens empty without displaying an error
History restoration is limited to 10 messages to avoid overwhelming the UI
Session continuity works across page refreshes within the same browser but not across different devices
technicalNotes: Add GET /api/chat/:profileId/history?sessionId=xxx endpoint returning last 10 messages
Defer the history fetch to widget open event (not initial page load) to avoid unnecessary requests
Webchat sessions already use sessionId in localStorage; use this as the message lookup key
rainbow_messages stores by phone field; for webchat, sessionId is used as the 'phone' equivalent

userStories.title: Intent coverage gap analysis: surface high-frequency unmatched patterns in admin
userStories.description: When AI cannot match an intent, the unmatched message content is not surfaced for review. Clustering unmatched messages by topic reveals systematic coverage gaps, allowing staff to add intents or KB articles for the most common unanswered questions, directly improving resolution rate.
acceptanceCriteria: Admin analytics panel has an Intent Gaps section showing the top 10 message patterns that triggered unknownFallback
Patterns are grouped by approximate semantic similarity or keyword frequency
Each gap cluster shows: an example message, count in last 30 days, and a Create Intent shortcut button
The Create Intent shortcut pre-fills the new intent dialog with the example message as a sample utterance
Gap analysis is scoped per profile (not aggregated globally)
Data is derived from message content stored when unknownFallback is triggered
technicalNotes: Store raw message text in intent_analytics when intent matches unknownFallback (add message_content column if missing)
MVP clustering: count word frequency across unmatched messages, return top 10 most common terms with examples
Add GET /api/admin/analytics/intent-gaps?profileId=&days=30 endpoint
Use existing intent editor component to handle the Create Intent shortcut with pre-filled utterance

userStories.title: Automated daily chatbot performance summary sent to admin via WhatsApp
userStories.description: Operators have no passive visibility into daily Rainbow AI performance without actively opening the admin panel. An automated daily WhatsApp summary to the admin number provides a zero-effort overview of conversation volume, resolution rate, top intents, and any active alerts.
acceptanceCriteria: A daily report is sent to a configured admin WhatsApp number at a configurable time (default 8AM local)
Report includes: total conversations in last 24h, AI resolution rate %, human handoffs count, top 3 intents, and fallback rate
Report is per-profile or cross-profile summary based on configuration
Report is only sent if at least 1 conversation occurred in the last 24 hours
Admin can enable/disable daily reports and set the delivery time in admin settings panel
Report delivery timestamp and status are logged for review
technicalNotes: Add a report generation function querying intent_analytics, escalation_events, rainbow_conversations
Schedule using existing cron/scheduler infrastructure
Send via Baileys existing sendMessage function (already used for escalation notifications)
Format as plain WhatsApp text using *bold* markdown, no HTML
Add daily_report block to settings.json: enabled, recipient_phone, send_time (HH:MM)

userStories.title: Webchat session idle timeout with configurable re-engagement message
userStories.description: Webchat sessions that go idle do not close gracefully or send re-engagement messages, leaving sessions open indefinitely and inflating active session counts. Best practice is a configurable idle timeout that sends a gentle re-engagement message before marking the session as timed out.
acceptanceCriteria: Webchat sessions idle for more than the configured timeout (default 30 minutes) receive a re-engagement message
Re-engagement message text is configurable per profile in admin settings
If the user does not respond within 10 minutes of the re-engagement message, the session is marked as timed_out
Timed-out sessions are tracked in the database and excluded from active session count metrics
Session timeout duration is configurable per profile (default 30 minutes, min 5 minutes)
Re-engagement and timeout apply to webchat sessions only, NOT WhatsApp (where Meta manages session windows)
technicalNotes: Track last_activity_at on webchat sessions (add column to rainbow_conversations or a webchat_sessions table)
Implement a lazy-check approach: check idle time on each incoming message rather than a polling loop
Send re-engagement via existing webchat message delivery mechanism
Add session_timeout_minutes and reengagement_message fields to webchat profile settings.json block

userStories.title: Profile configuration cloning: duplicate an existing profile as a starting template
userStories.description: Creating a new business profile requires manually recreating all routing rules, intents, static replies, KB files, and settings. A profile clone feature lets operators create a new profile from an existing one as a template, dramatically reducing setup time when adding new properties or brands.
acceptanceCriteria: Admin profile management view has a Clone Profile action for each existing profile
Cloning copies routing.json, knowledge.json, settings.json, and intent configs from the source profile
Cloned profile receives a new unique profileId and a user-specified display name
WhatsApp auth state is NOT copied (cloned profile starts without a connected phone number)
Admin sees a confirmation dialog listing exactly what will be copied before proceeding
Clone operation completes within 5 seconds and navigates admin to the new profile
technicalNotes: Add POST /api/admin/profiles/:sourceId/clone endpoint with { newProfileId, displayName } body
Deep-copy the source profile's rainbow_configs rows inserting with the new profileId prefix
Copy rainbow_kb_files metadata rows with the new profileId; do not copy actual KB file content on disk
Exclude whatsapp-auth/ directory and phone-number-specific settings from the clone
Return the new profileId so the admin panel can navigate directly to the cloned profile settings

userStories.title: Admin UI for per-profile WhatsApp frequency cap and rate limit configuration
userStories.description: Frequency cap rules (limiting outbound messages per user per day) exist as API-only settings with no admin UI. Staff cannot view or modify these rules without developer access, making the feature invisible to operators and preventing appropriate rate-limit tuning for different property types.
acceptanceCriteria: Admin Settings panel has a Rate Limits section showing current frequency cap rules per profile
Admin can set the maximum outbound messages per user per 24-hour window via a numeric input
Admin can enable or disable rate limiting per profile without any code changes
When a rate limit is hit, the admin shows a count of rate-limited users in the last 24 hours
Settings changes take effect within 1 minute without requiring a server restart
Settings are persisted to rainbow_configs (the existing config persistence layer)
technicalNotes: Add a rate_limits section to settings.json schema with max_messages_per_user_per_24h and enabled fields
Add admin UI component in Settings tab: numeric input for max_messages_per_user_per_day + toggle
Rate limit enforcement logic already exists in the codebase; UI connects to the same settings.json config
Add GET /api/admin/rate-limits/stats?profileId= returning count of users who hit the cap in last 24h
